gloss: Momotaro (folktale hero born from a peach)

definitions.gloss: Momotaro; hero of a famous Japanese folktale
definitions.explanation: The title character of one of Japan's best-known folktales: a boy found inside a giant peach who grows up to defeat a band of ogres on Ogre Island, aided by a dog, a monkey, and a pheasant he recruits with millet dumplings.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧のころ{桃太郎|ももたろう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}んだ→読む：00426_yomu⟧。
examples.english: I read Momotaro as a child.
Momotaro made a dog, a monkey, and a pheasant his companions.
Momotaro went to Ogre Island to subdue the ogres.

notes:
{桃太郎|ももたろう} is the hero of one of Japan's most famous folktales: an elderly childless couple find a giant ⟦{桃|もも}→桃：04382_momo⟧ (peach) floating down a river, and a boy springs from it when they cut it open. He grows up strong and sets out to defeat the ⟦{鬼|おに}→鬼：02184_oni⟧ (ogres) terrorizing the countryside, recruiting a dog, a monkey, and a pheasant along the way with {黍団子|きびだんご} (millet dumplings).

CULTURAL NOTE:
The story is taught to nearly every Japanese child and is often the first folktale foreigners learn. {桃太郎|ももたろう} is used as a byword for an underdog hero, and ⟦{鬼|おに}→鬼：02184_oni⟧⟦{退治|たいじ}→退治：14314_taiji⟧ ("ogre-subduing") is sometimes used figuratively for taking on a bully or a corrupt authority. {桃太郎|ももたろう} appears in place names, mascots, and product branding, especially around Okayama, which claims to be the tale's setting.
